diagram_candidates.kind: optional TikZ space-time cone and flux-face schematic
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example explicitly defines K={ (x,t): a_0<t<b_0, |x|<R(t) }, its two cap faces, lateral face and outward normal; the tip argument truncates a conical apex and estimates all three omitted flux or volume terms. A cross-section would make the face orientation and cap-versus-side flux geometry quick to verify.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Draw the time-space cross-section |x|<R(t) between t=a_0 and t=b_0, mark bottom and top caps, one lateral boundary and its outward normal (x/|x|,-c)/sqrt(1+c^2). In a second small panel, show R(t)=c(t-a_0) truncated at a_0+delta and the artificial cap whose flux, omitted lateral flux and omitted volume vanish as delta decreases. Label spatial dimension d and avoid implying a smooth chart at the apex.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The face descriptions and limiting estimates are explicit in the source; diagram value is editorial and uncertain, and is not needed for the proof.

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The proof constructs Phi(s,eta)=Gamma(s;sigma(eta)), proves its differential is invertible because the transport vector B=(a,1) is transverse to the Cauchy hypersurface, then transports the datum along characteristics. This is a concrete geometric coordinate map central to the local existence and uniqueness argument.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: In a two-dimensional space-time slice, show a noncharacteristic data curve sigma(eta), one transverse characteristic through each nearby data point, the base point eta_*, and the local image W. Label Phi(s,eta)=Gamma(s;sigma(eta)), B=(a,1), and g(eta) on the initial curve; use a tangent-plus-transverse-vector inset to show the independent columns of D Phi. Keep the drawing schematic for n-dimensional hypersurfaces.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: This is an optional geometric aid. The source states and verifies transversality and invertibility; the proof does not rely on a drawing.

diagram_candidates.kind: optional TikZ odd-shell versus even-ball support diagram
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The theorem contrasts odd-dimensional dependence on data in a neighbourhood of the sphere |y-x|=ct with an even-dimensional radial kernel K(rho,t) that is smooth and nonzero throughout 0<=rho<ct, including the centre. These are distinct support geometries worth making visible.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Use paired radial cross-sections centered at x: for odd n shade only an annular neighbourhood of the sphere boundary and label this as neighbourhood dependence, not pointwise dependence on the sphere; for even n shade the open ball and indicate a smooth kernel K(rho,t) with K(0,t) != 0. Mark rho=|y-x| and radius ct. Do not suggest that the odd-dimensional claim asserts pointwise sphere traces.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The distinction is stated and proved in the source. A diagram is optional and must preserve the explicit neighbourhood caveat.

diagram_candidates.kind: optional TikZ sector and nested keyhole contours
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The semigroup-law proof is driven by explicit sector geometry: two keyhole contours Gamma_1 and Gamma_2 with theta_1<theta_2 and r_2<r_1, their nesting, and which contour encloses the fixed resolvent pole in each inner integral. A complex-plane sketch can expose this map and the winding-number cases at a glance.
diagram_candidates.content_to_draw: Show the sector S={lambda != 0: |arg lambda|<pi/2+delta}, the lower and upper rays at angles +/-theta, the inner arc of radius r, and a truncated outer arc through the left half-plane. In a second panel show nested Gamma_1 and Gamma_2 with theta_1<theta_2 and r_2<r_1; mark lambda_1 on Gamma_1 outside D_infty,2 and lambda_2 on Gamma_2 inside D_infty,1, matching the two evaluations of the inner integrals. Keep contour orientation labels only if checked against the defining contour source.
diagram_candidates.mathematical_status: The nested-contour and winding claims are explicit; the diagram is optional and must use the cited Gamma(r,theta) contour convention.
